# Celo RPC through Chainstack

A single JSON-RPC endpoint for Celo mainnet, served from Chainstack's global nodes. The
upstream credential is injected by the gateway and never reaches the caller.

| route | price | body |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chainstack/celo` | 0.01 USDC | a JSON-RPC request, or a batch array of up to 2000 |

## Pay per batch, not per call

One settlement on Celo costs more in gas than several hundred RPC calls cost to serve, so
this endpoint is priced per *request body*, not per RPC call. Send a JSON-RPC batch and
pay once:

```json
[
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[]},
  {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"eth_getBalance","params":["0x…","latest"]}
]
```

A single (non-array) request is accepted and costs the same 0.01 USDC, so batch whatever
you can. The gateway counts every batch entry, including notifications without an `id`,
and caps the batch at 2000 calls. It also caps body size at 128 KiB. A larger batch,
a larger body, or one that is not JSON is refused before any payment. Fewer calls with
large parameters reach the byte cap sooner.

Every method costs the same, including `debug_*` and `trace_*`. The method travels inside
the body and the gateway prices by path, so it cannot tell them apart.

## Buying it

Quote first. The 402 challenge is authoritative, and the price does not depend on which
methods are in the batch.

```text
buy_pay_quote
  url:    https://gateway.usebuy.ai/chainstack/celo
  method: POST
  body:   "[{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",\"id\":1,\"method\":\"eth_blockNumber\",\"params\":[]}]"
```

Then `buy_curl` with the same url, method and body, and `maxAmount` from the quote. From
the CLI, an unpaid `curl` POST returns the 402; `buy curl --max-amount 0.01` performs the
paid retry.

## What comes back

The upstream JSON-RPC response, unmodified: a single object for a single request, an array
for a batch. Match batch results to requests by `id`. A JSON-RPC level error (bad params, unknown
method) arrives as a normal `200` with an `error` member per entry, and is **not**
refunded; the batch was served.

## Failures

Refused before payment, so they cost nothing and carry no `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`:

- `400` for a body that is not JSON or a batch over 2000 calls, `413` for a body over
  128 KiB, `405` for a paid request with any method but `POST`. An unpaid request with
  no body, by `POST`, `GET` or `HEAD`, gets the `402` with the price.
- `429` from the gateway's own rate limit. Wait for `Retry-After`, then retry.
- `503` with `paymentSettled: false` when the upstream allowance is spent.

Everything else arrives after settlement and was paid for. Any status Chainstack itself
returns, its own `429` or `5xx` included, comes back with an `X-PAYMENT-RESPONSE`
receipt, and so does a JSON-RPC error inside a `200`. Check for that header before
retrying a failure: if it is there the batch was charged, and a retry signs a new
authorisation and is charged again. When the response was lost or is a `500`, run
`buy receipts --resolve` before doing anything else.
